placements.why: The envelope's content — a standing rehearsal cadence for a rollback capability, justified by the principle that an unrehearsed rollback isn't a real one — is an organizational-strategy category about proving reliability through practice, not a fact belonging under any other org area. Nothing in the (currently empty) supplied strata covers validation/reliability practice, so this is a NEW top-level category, matching the ratified taxonomy's own 'Proof' category name.
placements.title: Operational reliability is demonstrated through rehearsal, not design.
placements.theme: Systems earn trust through recurring, rehearsed validation of their recovery and failure-handling capabilities.

placements.title: Rollback capability is only real once it has been rehearsed.
placements.theme: A recovery capability (like Atlas rollback) counts as real only when it is continuously rehearsed on a standing cadence with a clear owner, not merely designed or documented.
placements.why: src-2 states the governing principle directly ('a rollback we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have'); src-1 and src-3 enact it by establishing the monthly cadence that makes the rehearsal standing rather than ad hoc; src-4 completes the practice by assigning an owner accountable for it. Together these are the same recurring, future-feedable subject — not a one-time fact — so they form a single thematic leaf rather than four disconnected assertions. No existing leaf was supplied to reuse (graph structure is empty), so this is a genuine mint, homed under the newly minted Proof strata since the theme is squarely about proving operational reliability through rehearsal.
